subproblem.title: Euclidean coefficient norm of k-covectors is induced by a linear isomorphism onto ℝ^N (Simon 6.1.2–1.5, Fact A)
subproblem.statement: For all P, k ∈ ℕ there are N ∈ ℕ and an ℝ-linear isomorphism J from the space Covector (Eucl P) k of k-covectors on ℝ^P onto the Euclidean space EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin N) such that covectorEuclideanNorm α = ‖J α‖ (Euclidean norm) for every k-covector α.
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (P k : ℕ), ∃ (N : ℕ) (J : Covector (Eucl P) k ≃ₗ[ℝ] EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin N)), ∀ α : Covector (Eucl P) k, covectorEuclideanNorm α = ‖J α‖
subproblem.natural_proof:
Conventions. ℝ^P = Eucl P = EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin P) with standard basis b_i = EuclideanSpace.single i 1 = EuclideanSpace.basisFun (Fin P) ℝ i (i ∈ Fin P). A k-covector is α ∈ Covector (Eucl P) k (a continuous alternating k-linear map ℝ^P → ℝ) with operator norm ‖α‖; |α| := covectorEuclideanNorm α = (Σ_{I : Fin k → Fin P strictly increasing} α(b_{I(0)},…,b_{I(k−1)})²)^{1/2}. A k-vector is w ∈ NVector (Eucl P) k, a continuous linear functional on k-covectors. D^k(U) = TestFormOn U k (smooth, compactly supported forms with tsupport ⊆ U), D_k(U) = GeometricCurrentOn U k, M_W(T) = T.massOn W = sup{ENNReal.ofReal(T(ω)) : ω ∈ D^k(U), tsupport ω ⊆ W, |ω(x)| ≤ 1 ∀x} (massAdmissibleOn). CF(U) := {φ : ℝ^P → Covector (Eucl P) k : φ continuous, HasCompactSupport φ, tsupport φ ⊆ U}. All measures are Borel measures on ℝ^P; ∫_A f dμ means ∫ x in A, f x ∂μ (integral for μ.restrict A). Source: Simon, Introduction to GMT, Ch. 6, 2.7–2.9 (pp. 136–137), with Ch. 1, 4.14 (Riesz) and 1.17 (Lusin); this argument is extracted from the parent proof of slicing_mass_representation (its steps are cited as P1–P7).

This is Fact A of the parent proof (its conventions paragraph and step P2), made explicit.

Notation: for f : Fin k → Fin P put e_f := (b_{f(0)},…,b_{f(k−1)}); S := {I : Fin k → Fin P | I strictly increasing}, a finite set.

1. (Definition of J.) Let N := #S and fix a bijection σ : Fin N → S (Fintype.equivFin). Define J α := (α(e_{σ(n)}))_{n ∈ Fin N} ∈ EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin N). J is ℝ-linear because evaluation of α at a fixed tuple is linear in α.
2. (Norm identity.) ‖J α‖² = Σ_{n ∈ Fin N} α(e_{σ(n)})² = Σ_{I ∈ S} α(e_I)² (reindexing by the bijection σ) = Σ_{I : Fin k → Fin P} (if I is strictly increasing then α(e_I)² else 0). The tuple (EuclideanSpace.basisFun (Fin P) ℝ (I i))_i in the definition of covectorEuclideanNorm is exactly e_I, so taking square roots gives ‖J α‖ = covectorEuclideanNorm α.
3. (Values on coordinate tuples are determined by the increasing ones.) Let α be a k-covector and f : Fin k → Fin P. (a) If f is not injective, then f(i) = f(j) for some i ≠ j, so e_f has two equal entries and α(e_f) = 0 because α is alternating. (b) If f is injective, sort it: there is a permutation τ of Fin k such that I := f ∘ τ is monotone (e.g. Mathlib's Tuple.sort), hence strictly increasing because f is injective, i.e. I ∈ S; then e_f = e_I ∘ τ⁻¹ and α(e_f) = sign(τ⁻¹)·α(e_I) (AlternatingMap.map_perm).
4. (J is injective.) Let J α = 0, i.e. α(e_I) = 0 for every I ∈ S. By step 3, α(e_f) = 0 for every f : Fin k → Fin P. A multilinear map is determined by its values on all tuples of basis vectors (expand w_j = Σ_i w_j(i) b_i, so α(w) = Σ_f (∏_j w_j(f(j)))·α(e_f); Mathlib: Basis.ext_multilinear applied to the underlying multilinear map). Hence α = 0, and J (being linear) is injective.
5. (Dual coordinate covectors.) For I ∈ S let dx^I := wedgeCovectors k (fun j ↦ EuclideanSpace.proj (I j)). By wedgeCovectors_apply_det, for I′ ∈ S, dx^I(e_{I′}) = det M with M_{ij} := EuclideanSpace.proj (I i) (b_{I′(j)}) = (1 if I(i) = I′(j), else 0). If I′ = I, then M is the identity matrix (I is injective) and dx^I(e_I) = 1. If I′ ≠ I, then range I ≠ range I′ (a strictly increasing map Fin k → Fin P is determined by its range: its j-th value is the j-th smallest element of the range); both ranges have exactly k elements, so range I ⊄ range I′, i.e. there is i₀ with I(i₀) ∉ range I′. Row i₀ of M is then zero, so dx^I(e_{I′}) = det M = 0. Thus dx^I(e_{I′}) = δ_{I I′}.
6. (J is surjective.) For y ∈ EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin N) put α_y := Σ_{n ∈ Fin N} y_n·dx^{σ(n)}. By step 5 and injectivity of σ, (J α_y)_m = Σ_n y_n·dx^{σ(n)}(e_{σ(m)}) = Σ_n y_n δ_{nm} = y_m, so J α_y = y.
7. (Conclusion.) By steps 1, 4 and 6, J is a linear bijection, hence a linear equivalence Covector (Eucl P) k ≃ₗ[ℝ] EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin N) (LinearEquiv.ofBijective), and by step 2, covectorEuclideanNorm α = ‖J α‖ for every α. (Edge cases are covered: for k = 0, S consists of the empty map, N = 1, and the 0×0 determinant is 1; for k > P, S = ∅, N = 0 and step 4 shows that every k-covector vanishes.) ∎

Formalization note (not part of the argument): the expansion α = Σ_β α(e_β)·dx^β over β : Fin k ↪o Fin P, which also yields steps 4–5, is already kernel-checked as cmb_covector_eq_sum_coord_smul_wedge in commit 6c6b4b2753e8214a3e45619bb0b65d8d553557a5 of this repository (another DAG branch) and may be adapted as a template.
proof_key_steps: Index the strictly increasing I : Fin k → Fin P by Fin N and set J α := (α(e_I))_I ∈ EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin N), a linear map.
Reindex the defining sum of covectorEuclideanNorm to get covectorEuclideanNorm α = ‖J α‖.
Alternating + multilinear: α(e_f) = 0 for non-injective f and = ±α(e_I) after sorting; so α vanishes iff all α(e_I) = 0 (Basis.ext_multilinear), hence J is injective.
Coordinate wedges dx^I satisfy dx^I(e_{I′}) = δ_{II′} (determinant of a 0/1 matrix), hence J is surjective.
J is a linear equivalence (LinearEquiv.ofBijective) with the norm identity.

Source: Simon, Introduction to GMT, Ch. 6, 2.7–2.9 (pp. 136–137), with Ch. 1, 4.14 (Riesz) and 1.17 (Lusin); this argument is extracted from the parent proof of slicing_mass_representation (its steps are cited as P1–P7).

This is step P5 of the parent proof. Notation: M := #(Fin k → Fin P).

1. (Norm comparison.) For every covector α and I : Fin k → Fin P, |α(b_{I(0)},…,b_{I(k−1)})| ≤ ‖α‖ (ContinuousAlternatingMap.le_opNorm and ‖b_i‖ = 1), so |α|² ≤ M‖α‖², i.e. |α| ≤ √M·‖α‖.
2. (A linear functional.) For ω ∈ D^k(U) put S₀(ω) := ∫_A v(x)(ω(x)) dμ(x). The integrand is μ-integrable by hypothesis, hence μ⌞A-integrable (μ.restrict A ≤ μ). Since each v(x) is linear, v(x)((ω + η)(x)) = v(x)(ω(x)) + v(x)(η(x)) and v(x)((cω)(x)) = c·v(x)(ω(x)); by additivity of the integral of integrable functions and homogeneity of the integral, S₀ : TestFormOn U k → ℝ is ℝ-linear.
3. (Sequential continuity.) Let (ω_j) be a sequence in D^k(U) with TestFormOnConverges ω_j 0: there is a compact K ⊆ U with tsupport ω_j ⊆ K for all j such that, for every order m, iteratedFDeriv ℝ m ω_j → iteratedFDeriv ℝ m 0 = 0 uniformly on K. For m = 0, ‖iteratedFDeriv ℝ 0 ω_j x‖ = ‖ω_j(x)‖ (norm_iteratedFDeriv_zero), so for every ε > 0 there is j₀ with ‖ω_j(x)‖ ≤ ε for all x ∈ K and j ≥ j₀. For x ∉ K, ω_j(x) = 0 and v(x)(ω_j(x)) = 0; for x ∈ K, |v(x)(ω_j(x))| ≤ |ω_j(x)| ≤ √M·‖ω_j(x)‖. 4. (Conclusion.) S := ⟨S₀, step 3⟩ is an element of GeometricCurrentOn U k, and S(ω) = ∫_A v(x)(ω(x)) dμ(x) for all ω ∈ D^k(U). ∎

S₀(ω) := ∫_A v(ω) dμ is linear because each integrand is integrable.
If ω_j → 0 in D^k(U), supports lie in a compact K ⊆ U and ω_j → 0 uniformly on K, so |S₀(ω_j)| ≤ √M μ(K) sup_K ‖ω_j‖ → 0.

subproblem.statement: Let P, k ∈ ℕ, U ⊆ ℝ^P, μ a Borel measure on ℝ^P with μ(K) < ∞ for every compact K ⊆ U, and v : ℝ^P → NVector (Eucl P) k with |v(x)(α)| ≤ covectorEuclideanNorm α for all x, α, x ↦ v(x)(α) Borel for every α, and such that for μ-a.e. x there is α with covectorEuclideanNorm α ≤ 1 and v(x)(α) = 1. Let A ⊆ ℝ^P be Borel, W ⊆ U open and c ∈ [0, ∞] with c < μ(W ∩ A). Then there is a continuous φ : ℝ^P → Covector (Eucl P) k with compact support, tsupport φ ⊆ W, covectorEuclideanNorm(φ(x)) ≤ 1 for all x, and c < ENNReal.ofReal(∫_A v(x)(φ(x)) dμ(x)).

Conventions. ℝ^P = Eucl P = EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin P) with standard basis b_i = EuclideanSpace.single i 1 = EuclideanSpace.basisFun (Fin P) ℝ i (i ∈ Fin P). A k-covector is α ∈ Covector (Eucl P) k (a continuous alternating k-linear map ℝ^P → ℝ) with operator norm ‖α‖; |α| := covectorEuclideanNorm α = (Σ_{I : Fin k → Fin P strictly increasing} α(b_{I(0)},…,b_{I(k−1)})²)^{1/2}. A k-vector is w ∈ NVector (Eucl P) k, a continuous linear functional on k-covectors. D^k(U) = TestFormOn U k (smooth, compactly supported forms with tsupport ⊆ U), D_k(U) = GeometricCurrentOn U k, M_W(T) = T.massOn W = sup{ENNReal.ofReal(T(ω)) : ω ∈ D^k(U), tsupport ω ⊆ W, |ω(x)| ≤ 1 ∀x} (massAdmissibleOn). CF(U) := {φ : ℝ^P → Covector (Eucl P) k : φ continuous, HasCompactSupport φ, tsupport φ ⊆ U}. All measures are Borel measures on ℝ^P; ∫_A f dμ means ∫ x in A, f x ∂μ (integral for μ.restrict A). Source: Simon, Introduction to GMT, Ch. 6, 2.7–2.9 (pp. 136–137), with Ch. 1, 4.14 (Riesz) and 1.17 (Lusin); this argument is extracted from the parent proof of slicing_mass_representation (its steps are cited as P1–P7).

This is step P6(≥)(i)–(iv) of the parent proof, with the unit field written in the coordinates of the isometry J.

1. (Coordinates of v.) By the sibling theorem smr_covector_coord_isometry choose N and a linear equivalence J : Covector (Eucl P) k ≃ₗ[ℝ] H := EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin N) with |α| = ‖Jα‖; J⁻¹ is continuous (finite dimension) and |J⁻¹h| = ‖h‖. Let h_1, …, h_N be the standard basis of H and define u : ℝ^P → H by u(x)_i := v(x)(J⁻¹h_i). Each coordinate is Borel by hypothesis, so u is Borel. For every α, Jα = Σ_i (Jα)_i h_i, so α = Σ_i (Jα)_i J⁻¹h_i and, v(x) being linear, v(x)(α) = Σ_i (Jα)_i u(x)_i = ⟨Jα, u(x)⟩.
2. (‖u‖ ≤ 1 everywhere, = 1 a.e.) For every x, with α := J⁻¹u(x): ‖u(x)‖² = ⟨u(x), u(x)⟩ = v(x)(α) ≤ |α| = ‖u(x)‖, hence ‖u(x)‖ ≤ 1. If |α| ≤ 1 and v(x)(α) = 1 for some α, then 1 = ⟨Jα, u(x)⟩ ≤ ‖Jα‖·‖u(x)‖ ≤ ‖u(x)‖. Hence G := {x : ‖u(x)‖ = 1} is a Borel set with μ(ℝ^P ∖ G) = 0.
3. (Compact inner approximation.) Since c < μ(W ∩ A), c < ∞. The open set W ⊆ ℝ^P is σ-compact: W = ⋃_j K_j with compact K_j ⊆ K_{j+1} (e.g. a compact exhaustion of the locally compact second countable subspace W; concretely K_j := {x : ‖x‖ ≤ j, dist(x, ℝ^P ∖ W) ≥ 1/(j+1)} if W ≠ ℝ^P and K_j := closed ball of radius j if W = ℝ^P). By continuity from below, μ(W ∩ A ∩ G ∩ K_j) ↑ μ(W ∩ A ∩ G) = μ(W ∩ A) > c (G is conull), so there is j with c < μ(E) for the Borel set E := W ∩ A ∩ G ∩ K_j, and μ(E) ≤ μ(K_j) < ∞ (K_j is a compact subset of W ⊆ U). Every Borel measure on the Polish space ℝ^P is inner regular by compact sets on Borel sets of finite measure (instance InnerRegularCompactLTTop; MeasurableSet.exists_lt_isCompact_of_ne_top), so there is a compact C ⊆ E with c < μ(C) < ∞; thus C ⊆ W ∩ A ∩ G. Let d := (μ(C).toReal − c.toReal)/3 > 0.
4. (Lusin.) The measure μ is inner regular by closed (indeed compact) sets on Borel sets of finite measure (step 3), which is the regularity hypothesis of Lusin's theorem Poincare.SimonGMT.Chapter01.exists_isClosed_continuousOn_of_measurable (Simon Ch. 1, 1.17). If N = 0 then H = {0}, G = ∅ and C = ∅, contradicting μ(C) > c ≥ 0; so N ≥ 1. Applying Lusin's theorem to the Borel set C (μ(C) < ∞) and each Borel coordinate u_i, i = 1, …, N, gives closed F_i ⊆ C with μ(C ∖ F_i) < d/N and u_i continuous on F_i. Let C′ := ⋂_i F_i, a closed subset of the compact set C, hence compact; μ(C ∖ C′) ≤ Σ_i μ(C ∖ F_i) < d, and u is continuous on C′ (all coordinates are). Thus μ(C′) > μ(C) − d and C′ ⊆ C ⊆ W ∩ A ∩ G.
5. (Tietze.) u restricted to C′ is a continuous map into the closed unit ball B̄ of H (step 2). The closed unit ball of a finite-dimensional real normed space has the Tietze extension property (Set.instTietzeExtensionUnitClosedBall; alternatively extend each coordinate by Tietze's theorem and compose with the continuous retraction y ↦ y/max(1, ‖y‖)), and C′ is closed, so there is a continuous ũ : ℝ^P → H with ‖ũ(x)‖ ≤ 1 for all x and ũ = u on C′ (ContinuousMap.exists_restrict_eq).
6. (Small open neighbourhood.) Since C′ is compact and W open, choose r > 0 with K″ := cthickening r C′ ⊆ W (IsCompact.exists_cthickening_subset_open). K″ is closed and bounded, hence compact, and K″ ⊆ U, so μ(K″) < ∞. The open sets O_j := thickening (r/(j+1)) C′ decrease, ⋂_j O_j = closure C′ = C′ (closure_eq_iInter_thickening), and μ(O_0) ≤ μ(K″) < ∞. By continuity from above applied to the decreasing Borel sets O_j ∖ C′ (with empty intersection), μ(O_j ∖ C′) → 0, so there is j with μ(O_j ∖ C′) < d. Let O := O_j; then O is open, C′ ⊆ O, μ(O ∖ C′) < d and closure O ⊆ cthickening (r/(j+1)) C′ ⊆ K″ ⊆ W.
7. (Urysohn.) By exists_continuous_one_zero_of_isCompact (C′ compact, ℝ^P ∖ O closed and disjoint from C′) there is a continuous ψ : ℝ^P → ℝ with values in [0, 1], ψ = 1 on C′, ψ = 0 on ℝ^P ∖ O, and compact support. Then support ψ ⊆ O and tsupport ψ ⊆ closure O ⊆ W.
8. (The form.) Define φ(x) := ψ(x)·J⁻¹(ũ(x)). φ is continuous; support φ ⊆ support ψ, so φ has compact support and tsupport φ ⊆ tsupport ψ ⊆ W; and |φ(x)| = ψ(x)·‖ũ(x)‖ ≤ 1. By step 1, g(x) := v(x)(φ(x)) = ψ(x)·⟨ũ(x), u(x)⟩. Hence g is Borel (ψ and ũ continuous, u Borel); |g(x)| ≤ |φ(x)| ≤ 1 (hypothesis on v); g = 0 off O; and for x ∈ C′, g(x) = ⟨u(x), u(x)⟩ = ‖u(x)‖² = 1 because C′ ⊆ G. Being bounded, Borel and zero off O ⊆ K″ with μ(K″) < ∞, g is μ-integrable and μ⌞A-integrable.
9. (Estimate.) Since C′ ⊆ A and C′ is Borel, ∫_A g dμ = ∫_{C′} g dμ + ∫_{A ∖ C′} g dμ = μ(C′).toReal + ∫_{A ∖ C′} g dμ, and |∫_{A ∖ C′} g dμ| ≤ ∫_{A ∖ C′} |g| dμ ≤ μ((A ∖ C′) ∩ O).toReal ≤ μ(O ∖ C′).toReal < d (g = 0 off O and |g| ≤ 1). Therefore ∫_A g dμ > (μ(C).toReal − d) − d = c.toReal + d > c.toReal, and as c < ∞ this gives c < ENNReal.ofReal(∫_A v(x)(φ(x)) dμ(x)). With step 8, φ has all required properties. ∎
